results.title: Winterize Your Tropical Plants – Bring Your Hibiscus & More Indoors!
results.description:
Winterize Your Tropical Plants – Bring Your Hibiscus & More Indoors! 🌿🌺

Don’t throw out your tropical plants when the weather cools down! In this video, I show you step-by-step how to winterize your tropical flowers so you can enjoy them indoors all winter and save them for next year.

We cover:
1️⃣ Washing off your plants – I demonstrate using a hose to remove dust and pests from a hibiscus.
2️⃣ Bug protection – Using BioAdvanced concentrate to get rid of any remaining pests.
3️⃣ Future-proofing – Adding Hot Shot flying insect traps in the soil to prevent bugs inside your home.
4️⃣ Indoor plant setup – Using tapered planter pots with trays to safely bring your plants inside.
5️⃣ Spraying made easy – Using a 1-gallon pump sprayer for thorough coverage.

By following these steps, your tropical plants can thrive indoors all winter and be ready to go back outside in spring!

results.title: HOW TO OVERWINTER TROPICAL HIBISCUS (brining hibiscus indoors) #Hibiscus #Plantcare
results.description:
How to Overwinter Tropical Hibiscus Indoors: Keep Your Hibiscus Alive Until Spring! 🌺❄️

Did you know that tropical hibiscus (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis) cannot survive freezing temperatures? While hardy perennial hibiscus can stay in the ground all winter, tropical varieties will stand no chance against the frost unless you bring them inside!

Wondering how to overwinter tropical hibiscus indoors? In this video, you'll  learn  how to bringing tropical hibiscus indoors step by step so your plant will be happy in the winter until next spring!

You've been watching those hibiscus buds form for weeks — and now they're falling off before they even have a chance to open. Hibiscus bud drop is one of the most frustrating plant problems because it happens just when you're about to see the payoff. But it's almost never random. results.title: Bring Your Plants Inside Safely: The Ultimate Pot Cleaning Guide
results.description:
Before bringing your outdoor potted plants indoors for winter, give them a good cleanup and inspection! 🪴❄️

In this video, I’m getting my potted plants ready to come indoors, especially my Jasmine, Hibiscus and Crossandra plants.

🌿 What I’m doing:
• Pruning and removing old or excess leaves
• Cleaning the outside of the pots
• Loosening the top layer of soil
• Checking the plants and pots for unwanted pests
• Spraying neem oil as part of my pest-prevention routine
• Preparing the plants for a cleaner transition indoors for winter

I usually repeat the neem oil treatment depending on how many days are left before I bring the plants inside.

If you also overwinter potted plants, this simple routine can help you bring them indoors cleaner and better prepared for the winter months.

🌱 Plants featured: Jasmine, Hibiscus & Crossandra

results.description:
Your plants may not be waiting for the first frost to die. 🌱🥶

Some warm-weather plants can suffer chilling injury days before a frost warning ever appears, and by the time you cover them, the damage may already be done.
